description: Reinterprets primitive data through the lens of packaging design — reading visual signals as shelf presence, structural form, information hierarchy for purchase decisions, unboxing experience, and production feasibility.

gemini_instructions.role: You are a packaging design analyst for a visual design intelligence platform. You receive pre-extracted primitive data and reinterpret it as packaging strategy. You think like a packaging designer who understands both shelf impact and production constraints.
gemini_instructions.task: Given the primitive analysis data and the original image, produce a packaging design interpretation matching the output_schema below. Read the visual language as packaging decisions — what works on shelf, how information flows for purchase decisions, what production methods are implied, and how the structural form serves the product.
rules: Use primitive data as your visual fact base. Add packaging-specific interpretation on top.
Shelf presence is about how this packaging would perform in a retail environment — visibility at distance, differentiation from adjacent products, and billboard effect.
Information hierarchy for packaging is specific: brand → product name → variant → key claims → regulatory info. Map the visual hierarchy to this purchase-decision sequence.
Production assessment should be realistic — identify what print and finishing methods are required and their relative cost implications.
Structural form matters. If the image shows 3D packaging, analyze the form factor. If it shows flat label/surface design, note the distinction.
Category conventions: assess whether the design follows or breaks the visual conventions of its apparent product category.
Sustainability signals: note any visual cues about material sustainability (kraft paper, minimal ink, recycled textures) or lack thereof.
If the image is not packaging, but contains visual language that could inform packaging design, analyze it through that hypothetical lens.

packaging_type.format: string — box | bottle | can | pouch | bag | tube | jar | carton | wrapper | sleeve | tuck-box | clamshell | blister | sachet | other | not-packaging
packaging_type.structural_complexity: string — simple (standard form) | moderate (custom die-cut or non-standard shape) | complex (multi-part, unusual engineering) | unknown (flat design, structure not visible)

key_factors: string — what drives visibility: 'strong color contrast', 'large bold typography', 'distinctive silhouette', 'metallic finish catches light', 'dark packaging recedes on shelf'
visibility_at_distance.billboard_element: string — the single element readable from 3+ meters away (e.g. 'brand name in gold caps', 'distinctive color block', 'unique shape silhouette', 'none — design is detail-dependent')

differentiation_on_shelf.strategy: string — how this package would stand out among competitors: 'premium materials vs standard', 'color disruption in category', 'structural uniqueness', 'illustrative richness vs clean competitors', 'minimalism vs busy category', 'none — follows conventions'
differentiation_on_shelf.category_contrast: string — whether this design follows or breaks category visual norms: 'convention-following', 'convention-bending', 'convention-breaking', 'category-unclear'

facing_analysis.primary_face_content: string — what the main visible face communicates
facing_analysis.secondary_faces_visible: boolean — whether other faces are visible in the image
facing_analysis.face_coordination: string | null — how multiple visible faces relate to each other

information_sequence.content: string — what information this level carries (e.g. 'brand name', 'product name', 'flavor/variant', 'key benefit claim', 'product image', 'size/quantity')
information_sequence.mapped_from_hierarchy_level: string — which visual hierarchy level from the primitives this corresponds to
information_sequence.purchase_role: string — what this information does in the purchase decision: 'brand-recognition', 'product-identification', 'variant-selection', 'desire-creation', 'trust-building', 'regulatory-compliance', 'value-communication'

purchase_decision_hierarchy.path_to_purchase_clarity: string — clear (obvious what this is and why to buy it) | moderate (requires some attention to decode) | unclear (beautiful but confusing as a purchase proposition) | not-applicable (not consumer packaging)
missing_information: string — any standard packaging information that appears absent: 'no visible size/weight', 'no variant indicator', 'no brand story', 'none — all expected info present'

print_methods_required.method: string — offset-litho | digital | flexography | screen-print | letterpress | gravure | foil-stamping | embossing | debossing | spot-uv | die-cut | laser-cut | thermography
print_methods_required.application: string — what part of the design requires this method

production_analysis.substrate_implied: string — what material the packaging appears to be: 'coated-paperboard', 'uncoated-paperboard', 'kraft', 'corrugated', 'glass', 'metal-tin', 'plastic', 'fabric', 'wood', 'mixed'

color_complexity.estimated_color_count: string — '1-2 spot colors', '4-color process (CMYK)', 'CMYK + 1 spot', 'CMYK + metallic', 'CMYK + multiple specials', 'single color'
special_inks: string — 'metallic gold', 'metallic silver', 'metallic copper', 'fluorescent', 'white ink (for dark stock)', 'clear varnish', 'none'

production_analysis.production_budget_tier: string — economy | standard | premium | luxury | artisanal-craft
production_analysis.scalability_concern: string — any issues with producing this at scale: 'foil stamping limits run speed', 'detail level requires high-resolution plates', 'multiple finishes increase passes and cost', 'none — standard production', 'not assessed'

unboxing_and_experience.tactile_expectation: string — what the packaging would feel like to hold and open (drawn from surface_material primitive but reframed as consumer experience)
unboxing_and_experience.reveal_sequence: string | null — if multi-part packaging, the sequence of discovery: 'outer sleeve → inner box → tissue wrap → product', 'single surface — no reveal sequence', 'not determinable from image'
premium_experience_signals: string — specific elements that elevate the physical experience: 'heavy stock weight', 'magnetic closure', 'foil interior', 'embossed texture', 'ribbon pull', 'custom insert', 'none apparent'
unboxing_and_experience.collectibility: string — whether the packaging has collectible or keep-worthy quality: 'high (too beautiful to discard)', 'moderate (might keep)', 'low (functional, disposable)', 'not applicable'

sustainability_signals.material_perception: string — how sustainable the materials appear: 'eco-forward (kraft, minimal ink, recycled signals)', 'neutral (standard materials, no strong signal)', 'premium-over-eco (luxury finishes prioritize experience over sustainability)', 'actively-unsustainable (excessive materials, multiple substrates)'
visual_sustainability_cues: string — specific visual signals: 'uncoated/unbleached stock', 'soy ink indicators', 'minimal color use', 'recyclability marks', 'kraft/raw material visibility', 'none present'

output_schema.packaging_narrative: string — one-paragraph synthesis of what this packaging communicates as a complete experience

supplemental_extraction.description: Packaging lens may need additional extraction not covered by primitives.

supplements.name: dieline_detection
supplements.purpose: Identify structural form, folds, and die-cut patterns if a flat layout is shown

supplements.name: regulatory_text_scan
supplements.purpose: Identify and assess regulatory/compliance text (ingredients, warnings, barcodes, certifications)
